title: Things to Do in Ujjain: Mahakaleshwar, Bhasma Aarti, Ghats & Ancient Observatory
seoTitle: Things to Do in Ujjain: Mahakal, Ghats & Temples | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Ujjain: the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and its Bhasma Aarti, the Mahakal Lok corridor, Ram Ghat and the Shipra aarti, Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi and Chintaman Ganesh temples, Sandipani Ashram, the Vedh Shala observatory and Mangalnath.
dek: One of Hinduism's seven sacred cities on the Shipra river, home to a Jyotirlinga famous for its pre-dawn ash ritual and a host of temples and ghats.
searchIntent: Pilgrims and families planning one or two days in Ujjain, often from Indore, including the Bhasma Aarti.
intro: Ujjain, on the Shipra river about 55 km from Indore, is one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism and one of the four sites of the Kumbh Mela, known here as the Simhastha. It was also the capital of ancient Avanti and a centre of astronomy: the Tropic of Cancer passes nearby, and classical Indian astronomers used Ujjain as their prime meridian.

The things to do in Ujjain begin at the Mahakaleshwar Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, whose pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti is unique. Around it are the Mahakal Lok corridor, ghats on the Shipra, and temples to Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, Chintaman Ganesh and Mangalnath, as well as the observatory built by Jai Singh II.
One or two days is enough. October to March is the most comfortable time; the next Simhastha is expected in 2028.
quickAnswer: Attend the Bhasma Aarti (book in advance)
Walk through the Mahakal Lok corridor
Watch the evening aarti at Ram Ghat
See the lamp towers of Harsiddhi Temple

items.name: Have darshan at Mahakaleshwar
body: The Mahakaleshwar Temple houses one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and is unusual in that the lingam faces south (dakshinamukhi), considered especially significant. The multi-tiered temple sits beside the Rudra Sagar lake. Queues vary; general and paid quick darshan are available.
Phones and leather items are not allowed inside; use the lockers. Dress modestly.

items.name: Attend the Bhasma Aarti
body: The Bhasma Aarti, held before dawn every day, is a ritual in which the lingam is adorned with sacred ash to the sound of drums and chants. Entry is limited and must be booked in advance through the temple's official system, and a dress code applies for those entering the inner area. Some visitors can watch from a viewing gallery.

items.name: Walk through the Mahakal Lok corridor
body: Mahakal Lok, a corridor opened in 2022 around the temple, has large statues and murals depicting stories of Shiva, a musical fountain and light installations. It is lit up beautifully in the evening.

items.name: Watch the aarti at Ram Ghat
body: Ram Ghat, the oldest ghat on the Shipra, is where pilgrims bathe and where the evening aarti is performed with lamps and bells. During the Simhastha, it becomes the centre of the bathing rituals.
Boats can be hired on the Shipra, and small temples line the ghats. Sit on the steps before sunset to watch pilgrims float lamps and flowers on the river.

image.alt: Ram Ghat on the Shipra river, Ujjain
image.caption: Ram Ghat

items.name: Visit Kal Bhairav Temple
body: The Kal Bhairav Temple is famous for the offering of liquor to the deity, a tradition from Tantric worship. It is one of the most distinctive temples in the city.

items.name: See Harsiddhi Temple
body: The Harsiddhi Temple, one of the Shakti Peethas, has two tall lamp towers (deepstambhs) that are lit with hundreds of oil lamps on festival evenings, a beautiful sight.

items.name: Visit Chintaman Ganesh and Gadkalika
body: Chintaman Ganesh, a few kilometres from the centre, is an old Ganesha temple believed to relieve worries. Gadkalika Temple, associated with the poet Kalidasa, is dedicated to Kali.

items.name: See Sandipani Ashram
body: Sandipani Ashram is where, according to tradition, Krishna, Balarama and Sudama studied under the sage Sandipani. A stone slab bears numbers believed to have been written by the guru.

items.name: Visit the Vedh Shala
body: The Vedh Shala (Jantar Mantar), built in the 18th century by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Jaipur, has masonry instruments for measuring time and the positions of celestial bodies. A planetarium is nearby.

image.alt: Masonry instruments at the Vedh Shala, Ujjain
image.caption: Vedh Shala

items.name: See Mangalnath Temple
body: Mangalnath, on the banks of the Shipra, is believed to be the birthplace of Mars (Mangal), and many devotees perform rituals here to counter astrological problems.

items.name: See Bhartrihari Caves and Kaliadeh Palace
body: The Bhartrihari Caves are linked to the poet-king Bhartrihari, and the Kaliadeh Palace, on an island in the Shipra, has water channels built in the Mandu sultanate period.

items.name: October to March
body: Pleasant weather for temples and ghats; Mahashivratri in February or March draws huge crowds.

items.name: April to June
body: Very hot; visit temples early and late.

items.name: July to September
body: Monsoon rain; the month of Shravan brings the Mahakal sawari processions on Mondays.

byTraveller.text: Book the Bhasma Aarti, have darshan, visit Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi and Mangalnath, and watch the Ram Ghat aarti.
Mahakal Lok in the evening, the observatory and planetarium, and the ghats.
Leave early, have darshan, see three or four temples and return after the evening aarti.

oneDay: Attend the Bhasma Aarti at dawn, then have darshan and walk through Mahakal Lok. Visit Harsiddhi, Kal Bhairav and Sandipani Ashram before lunch, see the Vedh Shala and Mangalnath in the afternoon, and end with the aarti at Ram Ghat.
tips: Ujjain has a railway station; Indore airport is about 55 km away.
Book the Bhasma Aarti well in advance through the official system.
Crowds are heavy on Mondays, festivals and in Shravan.
Use lockers for phones and bags at temples.
Stay near the Mahakaleshwar Temple if you plan to attend the pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Ujjain?
faqs.a: Have darshan at Mahakaleshwar, attend the Bhasma Aarti, walk through Mahakal Lok, watch the Ram Ghat aarti, and visit Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, Chintaman Ganesh, Sandipani Ashram, the Vedh Shala and Mangalnath.

faqs.q: How do I book the Bhasma Aarti?
faqs.a: Through the Mahakaleshwar Temple's official website, in advance. Entry is limited and a dress code applies.

faqs.q: How far is Ujjain from Indore?
faqs.a: About 55 km, roughly one to one and a half hours by road.

faqs.q: When is the next Simhastha in Ujjain?
faqs.a: The next Simhastha Kumbh is expected in 2028.
